display.title: The Three Weeks: The Three Empty Walls, the Western Wall and 'He Is Watching'
display.summary_short: Three nightly Shema B'ni programs for the Three Weeks: the five calamities of Shiva Asar B'Tammuz, a king's painting contest, the Western Wall, the young Baal Shem Tov and a coachman who learns Who is watching.
display.summary_long: Three evening programs of Shema B'ni, joined in one recording. In the first, Rabbi Goldstein explains why there is no music: the Three Weeks have begun. He tells of the five calamities of the 17th of Tammuz, from the golden calf and the broken luchos to the siege of Yerushalayim, the end of the daily offerings and the breach of the city walls, and urges children to use these weeks to grow in Torah, mitzvos and tzedakah. The second program tells 'The Story of the Three Empty Walls': a king holds a painting contest, and the third artist arrives at the last moment with a surprise for his wall. It is followed by a short legend of how the poor people built the western wall of the Beis HaMikdash with all their heart, which is why it still stands. In the third program, young Yisroelik, the future Baal Shem Tov, meets a mysterious old man in the forest and explains his father's last words: fear nothing but Hashem. After a word about why we wear a yarmulke, a rabbi travelling with a hungry coachman teaches him, with a clever shout, that Someone is always watching. The recording ends with a reminder to care for the soul as well as the body during summer vacation.
display.lesson: Hashem wants us to earn His blessings through real effort; whatever is done with a full heart lasts. Hashem is always watching over us, so a Jew need fear nothing but Him.

date.hebrew: Early in the Three Weeks, in a year when 17 Tammuz fell on Shabbos and the fast was postponed to Sunday
date.note: 17 Tammuz on Shabbos: e.g. 5731, 5738, 5745, 5748 or 5751; year not stated. Summer vacation mentioned.

segments.title: Good evening and a healthy summer
segments.summary: Rabbi Goldstein greets the children and wishes them a healthy summer in body and spirit.

segments.title: The Three Weeks and the five calamities of 17 Tammuz
segments.summary: Why there is no music, why the fast was postponed, and the five calamities from the golden calf to the breach of Yerushalayim's walls.

segments.title: Tzedakah and a story tomorrow night
segments.summary: A reminder to give tzedakah every day and a promise of a story on the next night's program.

segments.title: The Story of the Three Empty Walls
segments.summary: A king holds a painting contest for three walls of his chamber, and the third artist arrives at the last moment with a surprise.

segments.title: You can't get something for nothing
segments.summary: Hashem has good things in store for us but wants us to earn them through Torah and mitzvos.

segments.title: The wall the poor people built
segments.summary: Each group builds one wall of the Beis HaMikdash, and the western wall, built with the whole heart by the poor, is the one that still stands.

segments.title: Hoping for the third Beis HaMikdash
segments.summary: A prayer that the days of mourning turn to joy, and good night until tomorrow.

segments.title: Young Yisroelik in the forest
segments.summary: The future Baal Shem Tov tells a mysterious old man why he is not afraid, and the stranger becomes his teacher.

segments.title: Why we wear a yarmulke
segments.summary: A Jew is never alone, and the yarmulke reminds us that there is Someone above.

segments.title: He Is Watching
segments.summary: A hungry coachman wants to take apples from an orchard and asks his passenger, a rabbi, to warn him if anyone is watching.

segments.title: An ever-watchful Eye
segments.summary: Hashem is always watching and protecting us; we thank Him by learning Torah properly.

segments.title: Summer vacation for body and soul
segments.summary: A reminder to learn something every day over the summer and to set a good example for friends.
